transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?

Well, I guess I'm here because... honestly, it's getting scary. What really scared me enough to make this appointment is that lately, I just keep thinking it would be so much easier if I just didn't wake up at all. It's exhausting. And then, sometimes when I'm driving home from the clinic—we had this golden retriever in last week, such a sweet boy, swallowed a whole sock, can you believe it? The owners were frantic. They always are, but you know, dogs will eat anything. Anyway, when I'm driving home after a long shift like that, I catch myself just staring at the road and wondering... what would happen if I just didn't turn the wheel? Just let the car go. It’s like, I don't even know where the thought comes from, but it's there.
Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, even if it felt good at the time?

Oh, yeah, definitely. There was this one stretch where... well, I was sleeping maybe three hours a night, tops. And I'd still get up way before sunrise feeling completely sharp. I was just convinced I didn't really need more rest, you know? Since I was up so early with all that energy, I actually started baking bread. 

Have you ever tried making sourdough? It’s a whole process. You have to feed the starter, and I actually named mine Clint Yeastwood. My husband thought I was out of my mind, being up at 3:30 in the morning folding dough in the kitchen. But I’d take the fresh loaves into the clinic, and the whole staff would just devour it in the breakroom. Well, except for Brenda, our receptionist. She’s gluten intolerant, so she'd just sit there drinking her herbal tea while we ate. She always buys those fancy teas in the little silk pyramid bags, you know the ones? I keep telling her she's spending way too much money on leaves and hot water, especially on a clinic salary, but she never listens to me. She just orders them online by the case. What were we talking about? Oh, right, sleep. But yeah, three hours was plenty for me back then.
During this recent period when you've been feeling this way, have you experienced anything like hearing voices, seeing things others don't see, or having beliefs that others tell you aren't true?

No, I haven't had anything like that. No voices or seeing things. I mean, the only voices I hear are the animals at the clinic, if you can call it that. We have this one patient, an African Grey parrot named Barnaby, and he perfectly mimics the clinic's phone ringing. It drives Brenda absolutely up the wall because she keeps picking up the receiver and saying 'Hello, Main Street Vet,' and it's just dead air. Barnaby just sits there in his carrier clicking his tongue, he knows exactly what he's doing. 

Birds are actually incredibly intelligent, a lot smarter than people give them credit for. My husband wants to get one, but I keep telling him that with our work schedules, it's just not fair to the animal. They need so much social interaction, otherwise they get stressed and start plucking their own feathers out. It's so tragic to see when they come into the clinic like that. We had a cockatoo last month that was almost completely bald on its chest... wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? 

Oh, right, hearing things. No, no voices in my head or anything. Just my own thoughts.

Over the past couple of weeks, how has your low mood affected your ability to do your daily work at the clinic and manage everyday tasks at home—are you still able to function, or has it become very difficult to get through the day?

Well, it's... it's been really hard. I'm just barely getting by, honestly. I've actually started making mistakes at the clinic, which is so unlike me. I drew up the wrong vaccine dose the other day, and thank God Dr. Evans caught it before I gave it. He was really nice about it, but I could tell he was worried. He's such a good boss, you know? He's been practicing for thirty years and he still gets down on the floor with the scared dogs. He has this one trick where he smears peanut butter on the wall to distract them during shots. Speaking of peanut butter, did you know they're putting xylitol in some brands now? It's an artificial sweetener, perfectly fine for us, but it is incredibly toxic to dogs. Like, life-threatening liver failure toxic. We had to pump a golden doodle's stomach last week because he ate half a jar of sugar-free Jif. People just don't read labels anymore. They just see "low calorie" and throw it in the cart. I always tell clients they have to read every single ingredient... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, how I'm functioning. Right. So, yeah, I'm messing up at work. And I'm avoiding my friends, too. I just don't have the energy, and I'm terrified I'm either going to snap at them or just start crying in the middle of lunch. At home, it's just... I can't do it. My husband has had to take over everything. He's paying the bills, making all the meals. He's even been staying up with me, just... keeping an eye on me when those dark thoughts about the car or not waking up get really loud. I just feel so useless.
